items.headline: Luxury superyacht Eagle Wings III partially sinks after fire at Sentosa Cove marina
items.summary: A 112-foot superyacht, the Eagle Wings III, caught fire at the ONE°15 Marina Club in Sentosa Cove on Sunday morning and was left partially submerged. The SCDF, alerted at about 8.10am, brought the fire under control within minutes, and no injuries were reported.

items.headline: Singapore orders platforms to block inflammatory online posts targeting its Indian community
items.summary: Police issued directions requiring YouTube, Facebook and X to block 14 posts pushing the claim that Singapore was being overrun by Indians. Digital Development Minister Josephine Teo said the content, traced to a likely China-based platform, does not reflect Singaporeans' views.

items.headline: Singaporean, 20, dies in Malaysia crash days before his NS passing-out parade
items.summary: A 20-year-old Singaporean man was killed on Malaysia's North-South Expressway in Johor when a lorry struck his motorcycle after it stalled in the emergency lane. He died days before he was due to attend his National Service passing-out parade.

items.headline: Pashinyan's Civil Contract heads for big Armenia election win in early results
items.summary: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's Civil Contract party led Armenia's parliamentary election with about 57 percent in early results, far ahead of Samvel Karapetyan's Strong Armenia bloc. The vote was widely cast as a referendum on Pashinyan's pivot toward Europe and away from Russia.

items.headline: Israel keeps up Gaza strikes as ceasefire talks resume in Cairo
items.summary: An Israeli strike on a Hamas-run police site killed at least five Palestinians, Al Jazeera reported, as Israel pressed attacks across Gaza on Sunday. Hamas and mediators from Egypt, Qatar and Turkey resumed talks in Cairo on the ceasefire's next phase.

items.headline: Drone strike on a North Kordofan market kills at least 11 in Sudan
items.summary: A drone strike on the main market in Abu Zaeima, a town in Sudan's North Kordofan state, killed at least 11 civilians and wounded dozens, a rights group said. No party claimed responsibility amid a surge of drone attacks across the Kordofan region.

items.headline: Update: WWDC opens with a Gemini-powered Siri overhaul expected
items.summary: Apple opened its Worldwide Developers Conference on Monday, with a long-delayed Siri revamp the most anticipated reveal. The assistant is reportedly built on a custom Google Gemini model and expected to ship with iOS later this year, in what several outlets reported would be CEO Tim Cook's final WWDC keynote.

items.headline: OPEC+ agrees a fourth output-target increase since the Strait of Hormuz closure
items.summary: OPEC+ agreed to a fourth straight monthly increase in its oil-output targets, even though the U.S.-Iran conflict is still preventing several members from pumping more through the largely shut Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude settled near $93 a barrel on Friday.

items.headline: Update: Zverev beats Cobolli in five sets for his first Grand Slam title at the French Open
items.summary: Alexander Zverev won his first Grand Slam title at the French Open, beating Flavio Cobolli 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-1 in his fourth major final. He is the first German man to win a Grand Slam singles title since Boris Becker in 1996.

items.headline: Update: Antonelli wins chaotic Monaco Grand Prix as Verstappen retires on lap one
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli won a chaotic Monaco Grand Prix for his fifth straight victory, with Lewis Hamilton second after a red flag and late crashes for Lance Stroll and Charles Leclerc. Title rival Max Verstappen retired on the opening lap with a mechanical failure.

items.headline: Update: England beat New Zealand by 115 runs to win the first Test at Lord's
items.summary: England beat New Zealand by 115 runs at Lord's to take a 1-0 lead in the series, bowling the Black Caps out for 138 on the fourth morning of a low-scoring Test. Ollie Robinson was named player of the match with figures of 7 for 77.

items.headline: Shreyas Iyer named India's new T20I captain for the England and Ireland tour
items.summary: India named Shreyas Iyer as its new T20I captain for the tour of England and Ireland, with Tilak Varma as his deputy. Selectors handed a maiden call-up to 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, while Suryakumar Yadav and Jasprit Bumrah were left out.

fun_fact.headline: The verb run has more meanings than any other word in the OED
fun_fact.body: The unassuming verb "run" has more distinct meanings than any other word in the Oxford English Dictionary. By the OED's count it carries over 645 senses - from running a race to running a business to a run in a stocking - overtaking "set" as English's most heavily defined word after the dictionary's 2011 revision.
fun_fact.source: Oxford English Dictionary; The New York Times

puzzle.title: Drilling the Cube
puzzle.body: Imagine a solid 3x3x3 cube assembled from 27 identical small cubes. A straight hole is drilled through the center of each of the six faces, continuing straight through to the opposite face - three holes in all, one along each axis. How many of the 27 small cubes are left completely untouched by any hole?
puzzle.approach: Picture which small cubes each drill actually passes through, and be careful not to double-count where the holes cross.
puzzle.answer: 20 small cubes. Each drill runs along one axis through the cube's center and passes through exactly 3 small cubes, but all three drills share the single central cube. Together they touch the 6 face-center cubes plus the 1 central cube = 7 cubes; 27 - 7 = 20 untouched, namely the 8 corner pieces and the 12 edge pieces.
